summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted with severe left-sided lumbar back pain radiating to the thigh. MRI revealed lumbosacral spondylosis at L4-L5 with nerve root impingement but no malignancy or infection. He also had elevated alkaline phosphatase, prompting further evaluation. Abdominal MRI and liver biopsy showed bile duct changes suggestive of obstruction, and ERCP confirmed a benign stricture at the bile duct anastomosis. A stent was placed to relieve the obstruction, with plans for removal in three months. He developed transient urinary retention due to narcotics, managed with tamsulosin. Hepatitis C viral load was detected (genotype 1a), and outpatient treatment was arranged. He improved with pain management and was discharged home with stable transplant function, instructions for follow-up, and a plan for HCV therapy and stent removal.
problems: Surgical operation with anastomosis, bypass, or graft, with natural or artificial tissues used as implant causing abnormal patient reaction, or later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of operation
